To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
rat hepatocytes express two types of ion channels, an inwardly rectifier and an outwardly rectifier.

(i) the activity of the inwardly rectifying potassium channel is regulated by the cAMP-dependent protein kinase; (ii) the activity of this channel is reduced by progesterone; (iii) the activity of an outwardly rectified chloride channel is not regulated by the c-AMP-dependent protein kinase and is insensitive to progsterone.
the cell membrane potential in rat hepatocytes is determined by the activity of an inwardly rectified potassium channel and that this channel can be modulated by hormones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of ion channels in hepatocytes.
the regulation of single ion channels in isolated rat hepatocytes and the effect of hormones on these channels.
the identification and characterization of single ion channels in hepatocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the outwardly rectified K+ channel is the most important channel for the regulation of cell membrane potential in rat hepatocytes.
the cell membrane is hyperpolarized by db-cAMP or forskolin by activation of a K+ channel.
the outwardly rectified Cl– channel is a candidate for the basolateral K–Cl cotransporter and the inwardly rectifying channel for the apical K+ channel in the hepatocyte.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inwardly rectifying 55-pS K+ channel and the outwardly rectiﬁing Cl– channel play an important role in the regulation of the hepatocyte membrane potential.
the cell membrane of rat hepatocytes is dominated by an inwardly rectified K+ channel, which is inhibited by progasterone.
the cell membrane of rat hepatocytes is mainly controlled by the inwardly rectifying and the outwardly rectified Cl– channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activity of the inwardly rectifying potassium channel is regulated by cAMP, while the outward rectifier is not.
ion channels in hepatocytes are not sensitive to Ca2+, but are sensitive to hormones.
the inwardly rectifying channel is a major determinant of the resting membrane potential of the rat hepatocyte.
